# Accounts

How a neighbor signs up, confirms the account, signs in (by email and password, with Google, or with a passkey), adds a passkey, changes or resets a password, and what a role allows. It is the site's largest security surface; it is not the admin panel. Fields, access, hooks and sign-in settings: [users content type](/docs/reference/content-types/users.md); the six pages: [screens](/docs/reference/routes.md).

## Screens

The six account pages, their routes and data are in the [screens reference](/docs/reference/routes.md); only `/account` is gated (by `requireUser`).

## Links between fields and flags (read first)

- `CURRENT_PASSWORD_CONFIRMED` (`domain/passwordConfirmation.ts`) is set in the request context only by `setOwnPassword` after the current password checks out (`data/session.ts`); `cms/requireCurrentPassword.ts` refuses your own new password without it. `NEW_EMAIL_CONFIRMED` (`domain/emailChange.ts`) does the same for `cms/requireConfirmedEmailChange.ts`. Context starts empty on every REST and GraphQL request, so no HTTP caller can set either.
- `SIGN_UP_CONTEXT` (`domain/signUpContext.ts`) is set by `createResidentAccount` (`data/signUp.ts`) so `cms/firstAccountIsAdmin.ts` skips it: the only automatic promotion to admin is Payload's first registration on an empty database; an admin can also set any role by hand (the role field is admin-only to write).
- `verificationResends` and `verificationResendsSince` feed `takeResend` (`domain/verificationResends.ts`): 3 resends per 3-hour window, stored on the account so it survives restarts.
- `verificationSetsPassword` is set by a resend and tells the verify step to ask for a password; `verifiedTokenHash` (SHA-256 of the used link's token) lets a reopened link answer "already verified" (`use-cases/verifyAccountFromLink.ts`, `use-cases/getVerificationLinkStatus.ts`). All four fields are server-only (`serverOnlyFieldAccess`).
- `googleSub` is Google's id for the person, never the email: it is how a returning Google sign-in finds its account, it is unique and server-only, and only a checked Google sign-in sets it: one that creates the account, or one that connects Google to an existing account, written by one conditional update only while the account has none (`linkSubject` in `data/socialAccounts.ts`, #1338); a Google create on an empty database is a guest too, not the first-account admin. `SOCIAL_SIGN_IN_CONTEXT` (`domain/socialSignIn.ts`) is set in that create's context so `cms/guestOnlyFromProviders.ts` forces `guest`, after `firstAccountIsAdmin`.
- `passkeyUserHandle` is the one random value every passkey of an account is made with, never the email or the id; it is server-only and written only while empty, so two adds at once keep one (`data/passkeys.ts`).
- `role` becomes `CurrentUser.role`, and the header's `AccountSummary.staff` (admin or editor), never the role itself (`data/mappers.ts`, `use-cases/getAccountSummary.ts`). A missing role counts as guest (`platform/payload/roles.ts`).
- Email links are built from the configured site address and the module's paths, never the request's Host (`domain/linkToken.ts`, `domain/paths.ts`, `cms/users.ts`).
- `src/payload.config.ts` hands `keepAccountEmails` to the verification module's retention task, so a confirmed address stays while an account uses it (`cms/keepAccountEmails.ts`).

## Behaviors and events

- Sign-up makes a guest that cannot sign in until its emailed link is pressed as Confirm on `/verify-account`, after the robot check, so a mail scanner opening the link verifies nothing. The link has no expiry (Payload's own verify), and a resend replaces it (`use-cases/signUpResident.ts`, `use-cases/verifyAccountFromLink.ts`).
- "Continue with Google" shows on `/login` and `/sign-up` only when `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are both set; with neither, nothing changes. `/auth/google` keeps its checks (`state`, `nonce`, PKCE) in a signed, ten-minute cookie that the callback clears after one use and sends the person to Google; `/auth/google/callback` checks the answer (`data/oauthProviders.ts`, through `openid-client`) and applies `decideSocialSignIn` (`domain/socialSignIn.ts`): a known Google id signs in; a new, Google-verified address gets a verified guest account and a sign-in; an address an account already uses sends the person to the password step (`/auth/google/connect`, below), so Google never takes over an account by its email alone. A locked, unverified or agent account is refused. A new account counts against the sign-up limits, and any failure goes to `/login?social=<code>` with a fixed message (`use-cases/socialSignIn.ts`, `ui/socialSignInMessages.ts`). Starting and finishing a sign-in are limited per connection only (`SOCIAL_SIGN_IN_LIMITS`), with no site-wide cap and no robot check: a cap anyone can fill would switch Google off for every neighbor, since a script can fetch a valid flow cookie and replay it for ten minutes. What remains is a botnet making many per-connection-limited requests, each costing at most one call to Google. The flow cookie is `__Host-` prefixed in production (Secure, `Path=/`, no `Domain`), and its flags and Payload's auth cookie's come from one helper reading `users.auth.cookies` (`data/authCookies.ts`, shared with "Keep me signed in"). A failure logs only the error's class name (from `openid-client` for a protocol failure), never Google's text. The session is Payload's own, so `/admin`, sign-out and lockout work as for a password sign-in, and it lasts the two hours Payload's default gives: "Keep me signed in" is not offered with Google. Signing in with Google proves no residency.
- Connecting Google to an account with a password (#1338, decision 0020), two ways, one write (`linkSubject`). At sign-in, the callback keeps Google's subject and verified email in `social-link-requests` (`data/socialLinkRequests.ts`; closed to every API, expired rows purged hourly by `cms/socialLinkRetention.ts`) and sets the flow's cookie again with only that row, signed under its own key, ten minutes; `/auth/google/connect` then asks for the account's password once and shows no email (`ui/ConnectGoogleForm.client.tsx`). The `connectGoogle` action takes the record once on every try, so a wrong password, a replay or another browser's cookie uses it up and Google has to be asked again; checks the password with Payload's own login (`isPasswordFor` in `data/session.ts`: limits and lockout, #140; a locked, unverified or agent account refused); finds the account by the verified email, never by input; refuses a Google id already on an account; writes the link; starts the session with `startSessionFor` (`use-cases/connectGoogle.ts`). Every refusal is one `failed` (plus `too-many` per connection, `SOCIAL_SIGN_IN_LIMITS`), so no answer says which check refused or whether an account exists. From `/account`, the "Google" card (`ui/ConnectGoogle.tsx`) shows only while Google is on: "Connect Google" is a GET form to `/auth/google/link`, which starts the same flow bound to the session's account (`linkAccountId`, in the signed flow cookie) and needs a recent sign-in, by the rule adding a passkey uses (`isRecentSignIn` in `domain/signInSession.ts`), checked at start and again at finish; the callback attaches Google to the session's account only, and only when the flow's account is the session's and the Google id is on no account, and Google must have verified the email, the same rule as signing in (`domain/googleLink.ts`). An old sign-in shows "Log in again", the one button the passkey card uses too (`ui/LogInAgainButton.client.tsx`); the card's "linked" message shows only when the account really has Google. An old sign-in, a taken Google id and any other failure come back as `/account?social=<code>` with a fixed message; a connected account shows "Google is connected". Either way a note with the time and no link goes to the account's address (`domain/googleConnectedEmail.ts`). `/auth/google/connect` sends `frame-ancestors 'none'` (`next.config.js`, `NO_FRAMING_PATHS`). The note says to change the password and tell us through the contact form; there is no way to disconnect yet (#1353).
- Passkeys (decision 0021): `passkeys` and `passkey-challenges` are written only by server code (`data/passkeys.ts`, `data/passkeyChallenges.ts`); admins read and delete passkeys, and no one reads a challenge. A challenge is taken once by one conditional update, a save only inserts a new credential ID, the counter only goes up, and deleting an account deletes its passkeys (`cms/deletePasskeysWithAccount.ts`). Expired challenges go in the hourly retention run. The rules are in `domain/passkeys.ts`. The feature is off unless `PASSKEYS_ENABLED=true`, read only in `data/passkeySettings.ts`; the relying party is the configured site address, never a header. Listing or removing them comes later (#1316).
- Adding a passkey (#1314): the "Passkeys" card on `/account` (`ui/AddPasskey.client.tsx` on the kit's `Form`, loaded on demand by `ui/AddPasskeyLoader.client.tsx`, so with the switch off its code isn't downloaded) shows only when `arePasskeysOn()` is true and the browser can make a passkey; with the switch off nothing on the page changes. The session must be a recent sign-in (`RECENT_SIGN_IN_WINDOW_MS`, the session's own start in `getSignInSession`, so "keep me signed in" never counts); an older one is asked to log in again, which signs out and opens `/login`. `getPasskeyOptions` limits the asker per connection and per account, with no site-wide count so no one account can switch adding off for everyone (`PASSKEY_OPTIONS_LIMITS`, `PASSKEY_OPTIONS_PER_ACCOUNT_LIMITS`), makes the options, stores a challenge for the account and sets a `__Host-` SameSite=Strict cookie holding only its row. `addPasskey` takes that challenge once, even when the sign-in turns out too old, requires it to be the session's account's and the session still recent, re-counts the cap right before saving, inserts, then emails the account's address the label and time with no link (`domain/passkeyEmail.ts`). A name is letters, numbers, spaces and a few marks, up to 60 characters, read after Unicode folding so a fullwidth or boxed look-alike counts as the plain character; look-alike modifier letters, variation selectors, enclosing marks and runs of more than three nonspacing marks are refused (`isAllowedPasskeyLabel`, checked in the card's form and again by the action), and `toPasskeyLabel` turns anything else into a space, so the email can't carry a clickable link or address (a look-alike letter in another script is still a letter). The only code that calls `@simplewebauthn/server` is `data/webauthn.ts`: discoverable credential and screen lock required, no attestation, one expected origin and ID, a `crossOrigin` answer refused, only `verified === true` counts, and every exception is the same refusal; the stored user handle is decoded to its bytes. Everything but `sign-in-again`, `cap` and `too-many` is one fixed `failed`. `/account` sends `frame-ancestors 'none'` (`next.config.js`). Both packages are pinned exactly; a bump gets the top-level review.
- Signing in with a passkey (#1315): on `/login`, "Log in with a passkey" sits under the form's "Log In" button, the verb the page already uses; the email field's autocomplete then names `webauthn`, so a browser that supports it offers the passkey in its autofill list too, and the button replaces that request when pressed. Both show only when `arePasskeysOn()` (the page passes `passkeys` to `SignInForm`) and the browser can use a passkey, and the code is loaded on demand; with the switch off nothing on the page changes. Email and password, forgot password and Google stay as they were, so losing every passkey never locks anyone out. `startPasskeySignIn` takes no input and names no account (the passkeys are discoverable), limits the asker per connection only, with no site-wide count and no robot check (`PASSKEY_SIGN_IN_LIMITS`: a cap a script can fill would switch passkey sign-in off for every neighbor; the challenge row expires in five minutes and the hourly purge bounds storage), makes the options and stores a challenge with no account, tied to the browser by the same `__Host-` SameSite=Strict cookie as adding. `finishPasskeySignIn` takes that challenge once before anything else, finds the passkey by the answer's credential ID, has `data/webauthn.ts` check the signature, challenge, origin, relying party ID, screen lock and counter, refuses a `crossOrigin` answer and an answer whose ID isn't the stored one, then requires the answer's user handle to equal the owner's stored one and the owner not to be locked, unverified or an agent (`decideUsePasskey`). Only then it records the use (the counter rises only when higher; a counter that should have risen and didn't is refused) and starts Payload's own session with `startSessionFor` (`data/session.ts`, shared with Google), honoring "Keep me signed in" through `data/rememberedSession.ts`: unlike Google's, a passkey sign-in can last 7 days. It counts as a recent sign-in for adding a passkey. Every refusal is one fixed `failed`, so no answer says whether an account exists or which check refused; a closed prompt gets no message, and an autofill request nobody started stays quiet unless a picked passkey is refused (`ui/PasskeySignIn.client.tsx`, `ui/passkeyMessages.ts`). `/login` sends `frame-ancestors 'none'` as `/account` does (`next.config.js`, `NO_FRAMING_PATHS`). The session works with `/admin`, sign-out and lockout as for a password sign-in.
- Payload's own REST verify answers 403 (`cms/verifyFromSiteOnly.ts`, on the collection in `cms/users.ts`); its GraphQL verify mutation fails a validation rule instead (`noVerifyMutation`, registered in `src/payload.config.ts`); the admin's verify page and forgot page redirect to the site's (`src/proxy.ts`).
- No answer says whether an account exists. Sign-up answers the same for a new and a used email, sign-in has one wrong-credentials failure (`data/failures.ts`), forgot password answers at once and sends in `after()` (`use-cases/requestPasswordReset.ts`). A failed sign-up email deletes the half-made account so the address isn't stuck (`data/signUp.ts`).
- A repeat sign-up for an unverified address resends the link after the answer, one resend at a time per address, within the cap (`use-cases/signUpResident.ts`).
- Sign-up and forgot password pass a per-connection limit, then the robot check, then a site-wide limit (5 per connection an hour, 20 and 30 site-wide); counts are in memory, one PM2 process (`use-cases/guardPublicRequest.ts`, `domain/requestLimits.ts`).
- Forgot password works only from the site's page (`cms/forgotPasswordFromSiteOnly.ts`); an unverified account gets no reset email, with the same answer (`cms/noResetEmailWhileUnverified.ts`).
- "Keep me signed in" stretches session, token and cookie to 7 days (`data/rememberedSession.ts`, `domain/sessionLifetimes.ts`); otherwise Payload's 2 hours apply.
- Changing your password ends your other sessions (`data/session.ts`); a reset ends every other session and sets no cookie, so the person signs in next (`data/passwordReset.ts`).
- Agent accounts cannot sign in with a password (`cms/noPasswordSignInForAgents.ts`); an MCP key is not a signed-in account (`getSessionPayloadUser` in `data/session.ts`).
- `requireUser` sends a visitor to sign in; `requireRole` gives a signed-in user without the role a 404 (`use-cases/requireUser.ts`).
- Account pages stay out of search results: each page sets `NOT_INDEXED` and the sitemap leaves out `ACCOUNT_PAGE_PATHS` and verification's `CONFIRM_EMAIL_PATH` (`src/app/sitemap.ts`).
- Server actions return fixed failure codes, never Payload's error text; the pages map them to fixed messages (`domain/types.ts`, `ui/*Message*.ts`, `platform/lib/messages/accounts.ts`).

## Shared pieces it uses

- `SlidingWindowCounter`, `HumanVerifier`, `ROLES` from `src/platform/lib`; `TurnstileVerifier` (`src/platform/turnstile`); role checks and `serverOnlyFieldAccess` (`src/platform/payload/roles.ts`); `runAction`, `runUseCase` (`src/platform/service`); `NOT_INDEXED` (`src/platform/seo`).
- Where it meets other modules (decision 0008): pages in `src/app/`, the collection, `noVerifyMutation` and the retention task in `src/payload.config.ts`, redirects in `src/proxy.ts`.
- Related notes: [verification](/src/modules/verification/README.md) (keeps a confirmed address while an account uses it, and shows `AccountOffer` after a contact confirmation; sign-up itself uses Payload's own verify, not its confirmer), [agents](/src/modules/agents/README.md) (an agent account is the owner of an MCP key, and sign-in is refused for it), [shared Payload code](/src/platform/payload/README.md) (roles, `runAction`).

## Rules and the tests that protect them

- Google sign-in: the rule `domain/socialSignIn.test.ts`, the paths `use-cases/socialSignIn.test.ts`, the protocol `data/oauthProviders.test.ts`, real accounts and sessions `data/socialAccounts.payload.test.ts`, the forced role `cms/guestOnlyFromProviders.test.ts`, the routes `src/app/(frontend)/auth/[provider]/route.test.ts`, the fields no resident can set `src/payload.config.protectedFields.test.ts`.
- Connecting Google: the rules `domain/googleLink.test.ts`, the paths `use-cases/connectGoogle.test.ts` and `use-cases/socialSignIn.test.ts`, the record and its cookie against real Payload `data/socialLinkRequests.payload.test.ts`, the link write `data/socialAccounts.payload.test.ts`, the password check and lockout `data/session.isPasswordFor.payload.test.ts`, the action `actions.connectGoogle.test.ts`, the card and form `ui/ConnectGoogle.test.tsx` and `ui/ConnectGoogleForm.client.test.tsx`, the routes and page under `src/app/(frontend)/auth/[provider]/`.
- Adding a passkey: the library's calls `data/webauthn.test.ts` and, with a software authenticator, `data/webauthn.registration.test.ts`; both steps with real Payload `use-cases/addPasskey.payload.test.ts`, the steps `use-cases/addPasskey.start.test.ts` and `use-cases/addPasskey.finish.test.ts`, the actions `actions.addPasskey.test.ts`, the cookie `data/passkeyChallengeCookie.payload.test.ts`, the session's start `data/session.signInSession.payload.test.ts`, the card `ui/AddPasskey.client.test.tsx`, the loader `ui/AddPasskeyLoader.client.test.tsx`, the page `src/app/(frontend)/account/page.test.tsx`, the header `src/app/apiHeaders.test.ts`.
- Signing in with a passkey: the library's calls `data/webauthn.signIn.test.ts` and, with a software authenticator, `data/webauthn.authentication.test.ts`; a good sign-in with real Payload `use-cases/signInWithPasskey.payload.test.ts` and every refusal `use-cases/signInWithPasskey.refused.payload.test.ts`, the steps against fakes `use-cases/signInWithPasskey.test.ts`, the actions `actions.passkeySignIn.test.ts`, the session `data/session.startSessionFor.payload.test.ts` (Google's tests from #505 moved there), the button `ui/PasskeySignIn.client.test.tsx`, its messages `ui/passkeyMessages.test.ts`, the form `ui/SignInForm.client.test.tsx`, the page `src/app/(frontend)/login/page.test.tsx`, the header `src/app/apiHeaders.test.ts`.
- Passkey store: the rules `domain/passkeys.test.ts` and the name rule `domain/passkeyLabel.test.ts`; real Payload: the challenge race `data/passkeyChallenges.payload.test.ts`, duplicate credential IDs, the counter, the handle and an account's delete `data/passkeys.payload.test.ts`; the switch `data/passkeySettings.test.ts`, the retention `cms/passkeyRetention.payload.test.ts`, who may read or write `src/payload.config.passkeyAccess.test.ts`, the forged handle `src/payload.config.protectedFields.test.ts`.
- Sign-up never makes an admin, Payload's first registration does: `cms/signUpFirstAccount.test.ts`, `src/payload.config.roles.test.ts`. Each guard: `cms/*.test.ts`.
- Own password and email changes need the flags: `cms/requireCurrentPassword.test.ts`, `src/payload.config.emailChange.test.ts`.
- Resend cap and window: `domain/verificationResends.test.ts`, `actions.signUpResend.test.ts`.
- Verify link, password step, "already verified": `use-cases/verifyAccountFromLink.test.ts`, `actions.verifyAccount.test.ts`.
- Remembered session lasts 7 days: `data/rememberedSession.payload.test.ts`. Roles gate pages: `use-cases/requireUser.test.ts`.
- Old residents became guests: `src/payload.config.guestMigration.test.ts`. Admin redirects: `src/proxy.test.ts`.
- Actions parse input again and use the session: `actions.test.ts`, `actions.changePassword.test.ts`, `actions.passwordReset.test.ts`, `actions.signUp.test.ts`.

## Boundaries

- Entry files: `index.ts` (types, paths, safe for the proxy), `server.ts` (use cases, forms, `requireUser`), `cms.ts` (collection, never server-only), `actions.ts` (server actions). Layers: `domain/`, `use-cases/`, `data/`, `cms/`, `ui/`; no other module is imported (`eslint.boundaries.config.mjs`).
- Never let a form or caller name the account: the account comes from the session.

## Decisions

[0003](/docs/architecture/decisions/0003-turnstile-robot-check.md), [0007](/docs/architecture/decisions/0007-email-confirmation.md), [0008](/docs/architecture/decisions/0008-compose-modules-at-the-app-level.md), [0020](/docs/architecture/decisions/0020-social-sign-in.md) (Google sign-in), [0021](/docs/architecture/decisions/0021-passkey-sign-in.md) (passkeys).

## Known gaps

- No code sets `NEW_EMAIL_CONFIRMED`: the change-your-email flow (#553) isn't built, so your own email can't be changed, admins included.
- `requireRole` has no caller outside tests: only `/account` is gated (by `requireUser`), so no page opens by role yet. The owner kept it on purpose (#728 audit, #756), so it is not a defect to file.
